mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the cost of capital declines.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns show no positive correlation with FEDFUNDS changes (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the direction of the relationship reverses (negative Rank IC) in more than 50% of the sample.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 5.0% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals a tightening cycle that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The rate threshold is crossed but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or the Rank IC for the threshold signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates a weakening demand environment that triggers equity sell-offs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce negative 20-day returns in at least 60% of the instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), a rising labor force participation rate (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly) signals labor market tightness that accelerates inflation, prompting the Fed to tighten policy and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The signal condition (UNRATE < 4.0% AND PAYEMS growth > 0.5%) is met but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, or the Rank IC for the combined signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) directly boosts corporate earnings expectations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as the demand outlook improves.
failure_condition: RSAFS growth does not correlate with positive 5-day forward returns (Rank IC < 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the relationship is negative in more than 50% of the sample.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% and remains below for three consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and inflation, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the Fed is pressured to tighten.
failure_condition: The unemployment rate remains below 4.0% for three months but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a rise in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates a policy response to inflation, which is typically followed by a market correction due to the expectation of future rate hikes, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint movement (FEDFUNDS decline and CPIAUCSL rise) does not produce negative 5-day returns in at least 60% of the instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth > 2.0% annually), a decline in residential construction (HOUST) signals a weakening housing market that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The late-cycle regime (GDPC1 annual growth > 2.0%) is present and HOUST declines, but S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, or the Rank IC for the combined signal is below 0.03.
